# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We want contributing to fak to feel safe, welcoming, and worth your time —
whether it is your first drive-by typo fix or your fiftieth kernel patch.
Autonomous coding agents are first-class contributors here, and the humans
behind every contribution (and every review) deserve respect.

## Expectations

- **Be kind, and assume good intent.** Most friction is a misunderstanding,
  not malice.
- **Critique claims, not people.** This project's core value is
  *verify, don't trust* — it applies to code, evidence, and benchmarks,
  never to a contributor's worth. "This claim needs a witness" is normal
  review language; "you can't be trusted" is not.
- **Welcome newcomers.** A first-time contributor who gets a warm, concrete
  review comes back. Point at the doc instead of reciting the rule.
- **No harassment.** Personal attacks, insults, discriminatory language,
  unwelcome sexual attention, doxxing, and sustained disruption are out,
  in every project space (issues, PRs, discussions, commits).

## Enforcement

Report conduct issues privately to the maintainer (see the repository
owner's GitHub profile) or, if you are comfortable doing so, in the thread
where it happened. Maintainers may edit or remove comments, lock threads,
and ban repeat offenders. Reports are handled with discretion.
